title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and an integer pivot, rearrange nums so that all elements less than pivot precede those greater than pivot, with elements equal to pivot in between.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and an integer pivot, rearrange nums so that all elements less than pivot precede those greater than pivot, with elements equal to pivot in between. Maintain the relative order of elements less than and greater than pivot. For elements i and j where i < j, if both are less (or greater) than pivot, ensure their new positions pi < pj. Return the rearranged array.
constraints: Place all values less than pivot first, equal values second, and greater values last.
Within the less-than and greater-than groups, preserve original relative order.
reference_solution:
def stable_pivot_partition(nums,pivot):
    return ([value for value in nums if value<pivot]
            +[value for value in nums if value==pivot]
            +[value for value in nums if value>pivot])
known_wrong_solutions:

    return ([value for value in nums if value<=pivot]
            +[value for value in nums if value==pivot]

def stable_pivot_partition(nums,pivot):
    return ([value for value in nums if value<pivot]
            +[value for value in nums if value==pivot]
            +[value for value in reversed(nums) if value>pivot])
hints: This is a three-way stable partition.
Collect the three relation groups by scanning nums in original order.
Concatenate values < pivot, == pivot, and > pivot.
Each comprehension preserves order within its group, and concatenation enforces the required group ordering.
editorial: Each comprehension preserves order within its group, and concatenation enforces the required group ordering.

tests.explanation: The less group is [-3], the equal group [2], and the stable greater group [4,3].
